ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Korean Commercial Act, Chapter IV, Articles 289, 317 and 330; Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (FTRA), Articles 2, 5-2, 5-3 and 5-4 and relevant Enforcement Decree provisions; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality; Financial Services Commission AML/CFT Regulations and KoFIU examination guidance.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Complete Certificate of Corporate Registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registry Office under the Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: issue the certified registration record from the court registry, notarize if required by the destination state, and obtain an Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consular legalization route: issue the certified record, notarize, obtain MOFA signature authentication, and then obtain Consular Legalization from the destination state's embassy or consulate in Seoul. The Apostille and Consular Legalization paths are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Tax Compliance Certificate of Tax Payment and No Tax Arrears)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service (NTS), local District Tax Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: obtain the tax compliance certificate from NTS, notarize the issuing officer's signature if required, and obtain a Korean MOFA Apostille. Non-member route: obtain the certificate, notarize, obtain MOFA authentication, and complete Consular Legalization at the destination embassy or consulate in Seoul. Never combine Apostille and Consular Legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution Appointing Incorporation Agent and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Chusik Hoesa and a licensed Korean Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: signed board resolution and power of attorney are notarized by a Korean notary; the notarized instrument then receives a Korean MOFA Apostille. Non-member route: after notarization, the instrument receives MOFA authentication and Consular Legalization at the destination diplomatic post in Seoul. These two routes are exclusive alternatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Articles of Incorporation of the Chusik Hoesa)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators and Notary Public in the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: articles executed by incorporators, verified by a Korean notary, and then apostilled by Korean MOFA. Non-member route: notarized articles are processed through MOFA authentication followed by Consular Legalization at the destination embassy or consulate in Seoul. An Apostille must never be followed by Consular Legalization or vice versa.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter after CDD/KYC Account Opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Korean commercial bank issuing branch after satisfactory customer due diligence under FTRA
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: bank reference letter on bank letterhead, notarized if required, and apostilled by Korean MOFA. Non-member route: bank letter, notarization, MOFA authentication, and Consular Legalization by the destination embassy or consulate in Seoul. The two authentication mechanisms are parallel and must not be combined sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every UBO, director, shareholder, signatory and authorized agent must be screened before incorporation and then continuously monitored. The mandatory screening matrix includes the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Korean governmental economic measures, KoFIU disclosure and PEP lists, and FATF high-risk jurisdiction calls for action. PEP screening covers foreign, domestic and international politically exposed persons as defined under FTRA. Any hit requires legal determination, enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, increased transaction monitoring, an audit trail and where warranted a suspicious transaction report to KoFIU. For low-risk online maternal and infant consumer sales, standard customer due diligence is applied but the customer risk rating is still documented and refreshed periodically.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (i-ONE); automated company name search and reservation module at www.iros.go.kr, operated by the Korean court registration service
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Korean Commercial Act requires a corporate trade name to be written in Korean with permitted characters; a Latin-script parallel name may be used if it is a faithful transliteration of the Hangul name. The four-tier naming convention is: distinctive brand identifier, precise business purpose covering online retail of maternal and infant care commodities, legal form suffix such as Chusik Hoesa or Co., Ltd., and head-office location. A foreign brand must be rendered into Hangul phonetic transliteration for the registered Korean name; the English name may be reserved as a secondary trade name only if substantively identical to the Korean name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation cannot be administratively extended; if the 30-day window lapses, the applicant must file a new name search and reservation application. Upon rejection, the applicant may submit a written objection and corrected registration filing within 14 days to the district court registration officer, attaching revised Articles of Association and a legal memorandum explaining absence of confusion with prior names. If the registrar maintains the rejection, an administrative appeal may be filed with the Seoul Administrative Court under the Administrative Litigation Act. The appeal must include alternative reserved names and evidence of publication search results. A Korean attorney should review the rejection reason before refiling to avoid repeated rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not per se unlawful under the Korean Commercial Act for the registered seat of a Chusik Hoesa, but Korean tax authorities and banks impose substance expectations. For an online maternity and baby e-commerce company, Korean banks performing customer due diligence under FTRA will generally reject a mere mailbox or shared director-only virtual address, requiring a physical lease, utility bills, local signage and verifiable operational presence. The NTS may also flag a virtual-only address as fictitious if tax invoices, inventory and payment flows disclose no physical workspace. A serviced office with dedicated desks, meeting rooms, a lease, and a visible regional presence is acceptable; a bare virtual office with no substance is not recommended and will complicate Stripe or PayPal onboarding and corporate bank account approval.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for physical inspection readiness: current lease agreement in the company name, utility invoices, office equipment, presence of directors or staff, registered signboard, business records, tax invoice issuance system, and third-party logistics or fulfillment center contract if inventory is held off-site. Quantified risk: a fully compliant low-risk online maternal and infant goods retailer faces an annual unannounced inspection probability of approximately 5%; where a virtual office or shared mailbox is used, the probability rises to 25-35% because the NTS and local municipal tax office treat notional addresses as a red flag. Unannounced on-site visits are legally permitted under the Framework Act on National Taxes and local tax collection procedures.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Korean Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended), particularly Articles 288 through 330 governing incorporation of a stock company (Chusik Hoesa), and Article 317 regarding registration of incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local Court Registry Office (등기소) under the Supreme Court of Korea, specifically the registry with territorial jurisdiction over the company's registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (정관) and the Application for Registration of Incorporation (설립등기신청서) filed with the court registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Under the Korean Commercial Act, there is no minimum paid-up capital requirement for a Chusik Hoesa. However, the total issued shares must be fully paid in at the time of incorporation, and the subscription price must be deposited into a bank account in the name of the company (or a designated account) before registration. The deposit certificate must be submitted to the registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (CHUSIK HOESA) ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN LIEU OF A MEETING PURSUANT TO ARTICLE 368(4) OF THE KOREAN COMMERCIAL ACT

WHEREAS, the undersigned directors constitute the entire Board of Directors of [Company Name] (the 'Company'), a stock corporation organized under the laws of the Republic of Korea;

WHEREAS, the Company has been duly incorporated upon the registration of its incorporation with the competent Court Registry, and the initial capital has been fully subscribed and paid in as required by law;

WHEREAS, it is necessary to adopt certain foundational resolutions to enable the Company to commence its business operations, including the subscription of shares, the establishment of banking relationships, the adoption of a registered office, and the appointment of statutory officers;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The Board hereby ratifies and confirms the subscription of the entire issued share capital of the Company, consisting of [number] shares of common stock with a par value of [amount] Korean Won each, for a total paid-in capital of [amount] Korean Won. The Board acknowledges that all subscription amounts have been duly deposited into the Company's designated bank account as required by Article 290 of the Korean Commercial Act.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board hereby authorizes the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer, jointly or severally, to open and maintain bank accounts in the name of the Company with any reputable financial institution in the Republic of Korea, and to execute all necessary documents, including account signature cards, resolutions, and agreements, for the operation of such accounts. The Board further authorizes the aforementioned officers to designate authorized signatories and to set transaction limits as they deem appropriate.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The Board hereby adopts and confirms the registered office of the Company as [full address], Republic of Korea, as stated in the Articles of Incorporation. The Board directs the Chief Executive Officer to ensure that all statutory notices, filings, and communications are directed to this address and that the address is properly registered with the relevant authorities.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The Board hereby appoints the following individuals to the statutory offices of the Company, effective immediately:
   - [Name] as Chief Executive Officer (대표이사), who shall represent the Company and have full authority to manage its day-to-day affairs.
   - [Name] as Chief Financial Officer (재무이사), who shall be responsible for financial management, accounting, and tax compliance.
   - [Name] as Auditor (감사), who shall perform the statutory audit functions as required by the Korean Commercial Act.

5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: The Board hereby authorizes the Chief Executive Officer and any other officers designated by the Board to execute, deliver, and file all documents, certificates, and instruments necessary to effectuate the foregoing resolutions, including but not limited to bank account documentation, regulatory filings, and any other agreements incidental to the Company's operations.

6. EFFECTIVENESS: This resolution shall be effective immediately upon adoption and shall remain in full force and effect until revoked or amended by a subsequent resolution of the Board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (공증인) in the Republic of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation (정관) in accordance with the Korean Commercial Act, including mandatory provisions such as the company name, purpose, registered office address, total authorized shares, par value, and the names and addresses of the initial directors and auditor. The Articles must be signed by all incorporators (subscribers) and then notarized by a Korean notary public. The notarization process verifies the identity and capacity of the incorporators and confirms that the articles are legally compliant. Ensure that the company name is approved by the court registry prior to notarization to avoid rejection. The notarized articles are a prerequisite for the subsequent registration step.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of all incorporators (passport or Korean ID)
Power of attorney if any incorporator is represented by an agent
Proof of payment of notary fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects in the articles, the incorporators must amend the articles and resubmit for notarization. If the name is rejected, a new name must be reserved and the articles amended accordingly. The notary will provide a written explanation of the defect, and the incorporators have the right to correct and resubmit within 10 business days without additional fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription and Deposit of Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Bank in the Republic of Korea (e.g., Kookmin Bank, Shinhan Bank, Woori Bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, the incorporators must open a temporary bank account in the name of the company (or a designated account) and deposit the full subscription price for the shares. The deposit must be made by the incorporators or the underwriters. The bank will issue a certificate of deposit (예금증명서) confirming the amount and the account holder. This certificate is essential for the registration application. The deposit must be made within the timeframe specified in the subscription agreement, typically within 2 weeks of notarization. The bank will verify the identity of the depositors and ensure compliance with anti-money laundering regulations. The certificate must be obtained in the company's name and will be submitted to the court registry.
required_dossiers: Proof of deposit (bank receipt or certificate)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deposit is not made within the required period, the subscription may be void. The incorporators can extend the period by mutual consent, but must notify the bank and obtain a new certificate. If the bank rejects the account opening due to incomplete documentation, the incorporators must provide the missing documents and reapply. Any delay in deposit will postpone the registration timeline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing for Incorporation Registration with the Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Court Registry Office (등기소) with jurisdiction over the company's registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 2 weeks of the deposit, the incorporators must file the application for registration of incorporation with the competent court registry. The application must be submitted using the official form (설립등기신청서) and accompanied by the notarized articles, the certificate of deposit, and other required documents. The registry will review the application for compliance with the Korean Commercial Act. If the application is complete, the registry will issue a certificate of incorporation (법인등기부등본) and assign a corporate registration number. The registration fee must be paid at the time of filing. The registry may request additional information or corrections if any defects are found. The registration is effective as of the date of entry in the registry.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of incorporation (signed by all directors)
Certificate of deposit of share capital
List of directors and auditor with their consent to serve
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
Proof of payment of registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or suspension, the applicant must respond within 10 business days with the requested corrections or additional documents. Common issues include incomplete information, missing signatures, or discrepancies in the articles. The registry will provide a written notice specifying the defects. The applicant can cure the defects and resubmit the application without additional fees, but the timeline will be extended accordingly. If the application is rejected, the incorporators may appeal to the court within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Compliance and Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) and the Company's Bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the certificate of incorporation, the company must complete several post-incorporation steps: (1) Register for business tax with the National Tax Service (사업자등록) within 20 days of incorporation; (2) Open a permanent corporate bank account and transfer the temporary deposit to this account; (3) Appoint the statutory officers as per the board resolution and file the appointment with the court registry if not already done; (4) Obtain any necessary business licenses (e.g., e-commerce license if required, though generally not mandatory for online retail). The company must also issue share certificates to the shareholders and maintain a shareholder registry. The bank will require the certificate of incorporation, the board resolution, and identification of the officers to activate the account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS rejects the business registration due to incomplete information, the company must correct the application and resubmit. If the bank refuses to open the account due to compliance issues, the company must provide additional documentation or choose another bank. Any delay in these steps may affect the company's ability to commence operations, but there is no statutory penalty if completed within the prescribed deadlines. The company can seek legal counsel to resolve any disputes.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity that begins any Korean VAT-registrable activity must file a business registration application (for non-residents) at the district tax office having jurisdiction over the place of business or appoint a tax representative if no domestic place of business. Required documents include the foreign entity's certificate of incorporation, proof of actual domestic place of business (lease contract), representative's passport or Alien Registration Card, and contract documents demonstrating supply in Korea. Upon acceptance, NTS issues a Business Registration Number serving as the corporate TIN and VAT ID. If the entity only exports goods out of Korea, it may also register as a simplified non-resident exporter for zero-rating and refund purposes. The application can be submitted electronically via HomeTax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean law does not allow a Chusik Hoesa to elect pass-through treatment. The only elective consolidation regime is group corporate taxation under Articles 76-2 through 76-18 of the Corporate Tax Act, available to a parent and its wholly-owned Korean subsidiaries; no hybrid mismatch election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold. Any entity supplying taxable goods or services in Korea must register for VAT. A simplified taxpayer threshold of KRW 80,000,000 applies only to individual small businesses, not to corporations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All registered VAT businesses must issue electronic tax invoices through the NTS HomeTax e-Tax Invoice system. Electronic tax invoices must be transmitted to NTS within the statutory period (generally by the day after the supply date for monthly taxpayers, or by the last day of the following month for simplified taxpayers). Since 2021, e-tax invoicing is mandatory for nearly all VAT-registered businesses. NTS performs real-time cross-matching of invoice data with bank and payment information; no separate physical fiscal stamp or anti-fraud clearance device is used, but data integrity is enforced through digital tax invoice certificates and prior approval of abolished invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated VAT applies to exported goods under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act, provided the goods leave Korea. Also zero-rated are certain international services, including qualifying offshore digital services and services with a place of supply outside Korea, and supplies of sea and air transportation. For e-commerce exports, the seller must maintain evidence of actual delivery out of Korea and the receipt of export proceeds.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration Certificate issued by Korea Customs Service)
Bill of Lading (or Airway Bill) proving physical departure from Korea
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Purchase Certificate proving receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under the Value-Added Tax Act, failing to substantiate zero-rating with customs and FX documentation triggers additional VAT at 10%, plus an additional tax of 0.3% of the tax amount for each day of negligent underpayment (limited to 10% of the amount) and a separate accountability of 40% of the unpaid tax for deliberately understated refunds. In cases of fraudulent claims using forged export evidence, criminal penalties may include imprisonment for not more than three years or a fine of up to KRW 30 million. The NTS also revisits refunds within the statutory audit window and may claw back refunded VAT with interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK), with enforcement and policy coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a free-floating KRW regime but retains substantial administrative controls over capital account transactions. Current account payments such as trade settlements, e-commerce receivables, royalties, and dividend distributions are generally freely convertible after truthful declaration to the registered foreign exchange bank. Capital account inflows such as equity investment, shareholder loans, and guarantee performance require prior or simultaneous registration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Foreign direct investment into a Chusik Hoesa must be reported through a government-licensed foreign exchange bank or through the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) before remittance, and the investing company then opens a domestic foreign-currency account to receive the funds. Korean foreign exchange banks act as reporting agents, and the settlement details feed the Foreign Exchange Information System operated by the Bank of Korea and MOEF. Profit remittance, including dividends to non-resident shareholders, is permitted in both KRW and foreign currency, but banks require proof of underlying earnings, audited financial statements, dividend tax filings, and confirmation that the remitting entity has no unpaid external obligations. There is no mandatory conversion of export proceeds into KRW; exporters retain flexibility but must comply with statutory filing and collection deadlines. Overall, the Korean regime is administratively liberal on current account items but requires careful documentary discipline for capital account liquidity movements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory surrender ratio for export proceeds in Korea. Statutory regulation provides that export proceeds must be collected through an authorized foreign exchange bank and must normally be received within 18 months from the date of export unless an extension is granted by the bank. Once received, funds may be retained in a foreign currency account or converted to KRW at the exporter's discretion. The mandatory conversion ratio is zero percent, and the exporter must file the export settlement in the Foreign Exchange Information System with the underlying customs export declaration.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW), Foreign Currency Account, and FDI Proceeds Receipt Account
Business Current Account, Export Proceeds Collection Account, and E-commerce Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account and General Operating Account for Cross-border Receipts
Import and Export Settlement Account, KRW Operating Account, and Brokerage Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low standalone viability. Stripe and PayPal card acquiring is feasible as payment collection rails for Korean e-commerce, but an offshore fintech EMI legally cannot open a KRW-denominated deposit account, provide corporate treasury services, or clear domestic Korean won payments without licensing by the Financial Services Commission and participation in the Korean payment infrastructure. The only compliant approach is to connect Stripe or PayPal settlements to a local Tier-1 commercial bank account and use the licensed bank for FX conversion, wire routing, and outbound disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Chusik Hoesa, the statutory representative or an authorized signatory with a certified and apostilled Korean or Korean-consular power of attorney must appear in person at the bank branch for an onboarding interview. Remote account opening for non-resident directors is generally not permitted. All statutory directors must present valid passports, visa or alien registration documentation if applicable, and must sign the bank mandate. A remote consular proxy opening is not a standard product and is normally rejected without a live in-branch or bank-approved notarized signing session.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shell corporation red flag triggered by low initial capital, a Chusik Hoesa structure, and non-resident shareholder concentration with no visible local business substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the certified Certificate of Incorporation, Korean Articles of Incorporation, shareholder register, board resolution appointing officers, audited or notarized financial statements of the ultimate parent, 12-month projected e-commerce cash flow, warehouse or fulfillment service agreements in Korea, and a signed organic compliance declaration covering all beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for injected share capital or mismatched remitter information on inbound SWIFT wires.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the FDI Registration Certificate obtained through KOTRA or the chosen bank, signed source-of-funds letters for each remitting entity, six months of bank statements from the remitter, board minutes authorizing the capital increase, share subscription agreements, and remitter identification matching the foreign exchange remittance application precisely.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty or trade-based money laundering exposure caused by cross-border suppliers of maternity and baby goods transacting through high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide entity due diligence files for every supplier, signed commercial purchase orders, customs import declarations from Korean Customs Service, bills of lading or courier tracking exports, insurance certificates, detailed commercial invoices, and sanctions and PEP screening results for all transaction parties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transfer pricing or intangible leakages arising from payments to overseas affiliate e-commerce platforms for marketing, cloud services, or royalty arrangements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare Korean transfer pricing master file and local file, OECD country-by-country report if applicable, technology licensing contracts, arm's length benchmarking study for platform commissions, breakdown of cloud and advertising costs, and evidence that all cross-border payments have valid withholding tax filings and economic substance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity capital must enter through the Foreign Direct Investment process. File the FDI registration through an authorized foreign exchange bank or KOTRA, obtain the FDI Registration Certificate, and then open a domestic foreign currency account or KRW process account under the certificate. Incoming remittances should be sent via SWIFT MT103 with the sender name matching the registered foreign investor and the FDI certificate number referenced in the remittance instructions. The bank will record the transaction in the Foreign Exchange Information System and issue a Foreign Exchange Report Number. After receipt, the Chusik Hoesa must issue the corresponding shares and arrange an external auditor's capital verification report confirming full subscription and contribution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for standard open-account supplier payments covering maternity and baby commodity imports. For goods requiring bank undertaking, use commercial documentary letters of credit opened by the Korean bank via MT700 series messages. For transaction-controlled settlement, use documentary collections with shipping documents presented on DP or DA terms. All outbound trade disbursements must be supported by underlying invoices, customs declarations, transport documents, and a valid foreign exchange purpose code. Stripe or PayPal payouts should be consolidated into the local KRW account and then converted and settled through the licensed bank rather than routed offshore.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable KRW forward contracts executed with Korean licensed banks for confirmed trade and investment exposures
Cross-currency swaps between KRW and USD for long-term balance sheet hedging of FDI or shareholder loans
Deterministic premium fx options including plain vanilla options with underlying transaction evidence

Offshore non-deliverable forwards restricted; domestic entities may only access NDFs through onshore banks for hedge capacity underlying approved cross-border trades, never for speculative naked positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) approval of financial statements and corporate housekeeping resolutions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders in general meeting; minutes retained in the statutory corporate minute book; no government filing required unless the company is externally audited
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By June 30 following the December 31 fiscal year-end (within 6 months of the fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the AGM within the statutory window exposes each director to a fine of up to KRW 5,000,000 (approx. USD 3,800) under Article 635 of the Korean Commercial Act; resolutions may still be valid if subsequently passed, but repeated non-compliance may lead to court-ordered dismissal of directors and administrative dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and financial statement annexure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 of the following calendar year for December 31 fiscal year-end; extended to June 30 if an independent external audit is statutorily required or if the corporation has foreign-source income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a non-return penalty of 20% of the unpaid corporate income tax; understatement triggers a 10% deficiency penalty; late payment accrues interest of 0.022% per day (about 8.03% annually) until fully paid; tax evasion referrals to the prosecutor can lead to criminal fines and imprisonment. Persistent non-filing may cause the NTS to assess taxes on an estimated basis and to administratively close the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate resident tax annual return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: City/County/District local government tax administration office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By May 31 of the following calendar year for the preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If unpaid, a late-payment penalty of 3% per month (capped at 60% of the tax due) applies under the Local Tax Act; the local government may issue a demand notice, seize bank accounts, and auction property. Failure to file may also subject the representative to a fine up to KRW 1,000,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent statutory audit report filing with electronic disclosure system (if audit threshold triggered)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the ordinary general shareholders' meeting, and in no event later than June 30 following the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the statutory audit report within the deadline may subject the company to administrative fines up to KRW 50,000,000 (approx. USD 38,000); the auditor may be sanctioned by the FSS; unaudited financial statements may be voided for tax filing purposes, and directors can be personally liable for resulting tax and default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-invested enterprise annual report (only if non-resident ownership qualifies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Invest KOREA / Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 days after the end of each fiscal year (by January 20 for December year-end) for a company registered as a foreign-invested enterprise under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual foreign-invested enterprise report may result in an administrative fine up to KRW 1,000,000 (approx. USD 760), downgrading or revocation of foreign investment registration, and possible restrictions on dividend remittance and extension of visa status for investors.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 2 of the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies (and its Enforcement Decree), a Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily subject to an independent certified CPA audit if, as at the preceding fiscal year-end or current fiscal year, any of the following quantitative thresholds is met: (i) total assets equal or exceed KRW 10,000,000,000 (approx. USD 7.6 million); (ii) annual net turnover equals or exceeds KRW 20,000,000,000 (approx. USD 15.2 million); (iii) average number of full-time employees during the year equals or exceeds 300; (iv) the company is listed on a Korean stock exchange (KOSPI, KOSDAQ, or KONEX); (v) the company has issued securities by public offering or is a designated public-interest entity; (vi) the company is a financial institution, insurance company, or hedge fund manager; or (vii) the company has outstanding borrowings from financial institutions equal to or exceeding KRW 1,000,000,000 (approx. USD 760,000) with a balance-sheet total exceeding a lower threshold prescribed by Presidential Decree. Companies with total assets below KRW 500,000,000 (approx. USD 380,000) may apply for exemption from mandatory audit by adopting shareholders' approval and notifying the regulator.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Listed companies and financial entities must apply K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards); unlisted Chusik Hoesas may apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP), including the Korean SMEs' Accounting Standards, in accordance with the Act on External Audit and the Corporate Tax Act. Voluntary full K-IFRS adoption is also permitted for any Korean entity.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Korean Financial Transaction Reports Act and AML compliance rules, a Chusik Hoesa must identify and record its beneficial owner(s) (natural persons who directly or indirectly hold at least 25% of shares or exercise actual control) and provide such information to financial institutions and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit upon request. There is no separate annual UBO filing for ordinary non-audited companies; however, the company must annually confirm its UBO schedule at the ordinary general meeting and keep the corporate books updated. For any share transfer, director change, or registered-office change, the company must file an amendment with the local district court commercial registration bureau within 30 days. If the company is a foreign-invested enterprise (foreign investor holds at least 10% of shares or invested KRW 100 million or more), it must file a foreign-invested enterprise annual report with Invest KOREA/MOTIE within 20 days after the fiscal year-end and also report material UBO or equity changes within 60 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges/Mortgages (if secured debentures or collateral rights exist)
Corporate Minute Book of shareholders' and directors' meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - USD 2,500 per year for registered office and corporate secretarial agent services in Seoul; USD 300 - USD 1,500 in other provinces
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 25,000 for a certified CPA audit under K-IFRS or K-GAAP for a mid-sized Chusik Hoesa with active e-commerce operations; simplified small-company audits may cost USD 3,500 - USD 8,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national top marginal corporate income tax rate under the Corporate Tax Act, plus 10% local
